steps.body: The single marks finish with 7, 8, 9. Nine is the last amount one mark can name — the next number will need two.
steps.narration: The single marks finish with 7, 8, 9. Nine is the last amount one mark can name — the next number will need two.

widget.prompt: Build the amount the numeral 8 promises.

commonCounts.feedback: Seven is one short of the promise; the mark 8 names one more.
Nine overshoots; the mark 8 stops the count at eight.

widget.missFeedback: Match the mark exactly: eight dots, then stop.
widget.successFeedback: Eight — the mark's double loop names this exact count.

predict.prompt: What comes after 9, the last single mark?
predict.reveal: Counting never ends; the writing system simply switches to two-mark numerals at ten.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw write 789.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw write 789.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

explanationVariants: Write it the right way round.

widget.prompt: A numeral written backwards, like a flipped 3 — what is the risk?

options.label: It may be misread or look like another mark
options.feedback: Correct — numerals are shapes with a direction; flipping one blurs its identity to a reader.

options.label: The amount it names changes
options.feedback: The writer still MEANS three; the danger is the reader, who sees an unclear mark.

options.label: Nothing — any direction works
options.feedback: Direction is part of the shape: readers rely on it to tell numerals apart.

options.label: The paper must be thrown away
options.feedback: Just write it again the right way round — practice, not punishment.

widget.prompt: Put the check routine for a readable numeral in order.

misorderFeedback.feedback: The final step cannot come first. Begin with the amount or starting point, then finish the numeral.

widget.missFeedback: Build the sequence in this order: Write the numeral, then Check its direction, then Read the intended number.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — write, check the direction, then confirm the numeral can be read.

widget.prompt: A seven-bead string needs a numeral tag. Which tag is exact?

options.feedback: Correct — the numeral 7 is the written name for a group of exactly 7.
8 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 7.
6 promises fewer dots than the group holds; the count reaches 7.
9 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 7.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 8? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 8 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 7.
6 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 8 to reach 7.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 8: you land on 7.
widget.successFeedback: 7 — the numeral written just before 8 names one less.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 8 reaches 7.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 8 means a single hop back, stopping on 7.

hints: Last number said, first mark written.

widget.prompt: Look at the ten-frame flash and choose the matching numeral.

commonPicks.feedback: 7 misses 1 of the visible dots. Group the dots, then count the full group as 8.
9 counts 1 extra. Touch each dot once in your mind — the group holds 8.

widget.missFeedback: Watch again and group the ten-frame: it shows 8 dots.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 8! The ten-frame and numeral agree.
